newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turk court adjourns in pro-Kurd rebel flag case.
newsitem.headline: Turk court adjourns in pro-Kurd rebel flag case.

text.p: A state security court adjourned the trial of 13 people charged with links to Kurdish separatist rebels and allowed 12 of them to go free pending the court's verdict, lawyers for the accused said.

The 13 were among 47 people arrested at a congress of the pro-Kurdish Peoples' Democratic Party (HADEP) last June when the Turkish flag was torn down by youths and replaced with banners of the outlawed Kurdistan Workers Party (PKK).
"Twelve of the 13 accused have been set free pending the verdict," defense lawyer Yusuf Alatas said after the hearing.
The state security court in Ankara was expected to give a verdict on Monday, but adjourned the trial without giving a date for the next hearing.
Families outside the court welcomed the decision to release the 12 who have been in jail since their arrest last June.
Faysal Akcan, the youth accused of draping the PKK flag from the balcony of the conference hall, was remanded in custody until the verdict.
Many of the accused, charged in September, face up to 22-1/2 years in jail under article 168 of the Turkish Penal Code if found guilty.

HADEP was formed in 1994 after another Kurdish party was closed by the constitutional court for alleged separatism and 13 of its deputies were expelled from parliament. Six of the MPs were jailed for links with the PKK.
More than 22,000 people have died in the 12-year conflict between the Turkish security forces and PKK rebels who are fighting for independence or autonomy in the mainly Kurdish southeast of Turkey.
